note: Word family: jeune (adj) → jeunesse (noun). Reinforces both adjective and noun forms for expressing youth.
Word family from travail (work): travailler (verb) → travailleur (noun). Inseparable derivation aids memory and contextual use.
Common confusion point for learners: entendre (hear) vs attendre (wait). Both similar form but opposite meanings.
Word family: mettre is the root, promettre = pro + mettre. Understanding prefix composition clarifies derived meanings (promise = put forth).

members.gloss: to put; to place; to set

note: Semantic chain: permettre makes something possible, yielding permission as result. Reinforces 'to allow' → 'permitted' → 'possible'.
Word family: devenir = de + venir. Prefix composition aids understanding of 'to become'.
Spatial motion verbs: partir (to leave) opposes arriver/venir (to arrive). Forms directional pair for movement contexts.
Logical connectives: ou presents alternatives, mais introduces contrast or correction. Both essential for sentence construction.
Spatial demonstratives: ici (here) vs là/là-bas (there). Spatial opposition aids learning deixis and location reference.
Existential quantifiers: rien (nothing) vs quelque chose (something) vs tout (everything). Oppositions reinforce semantic scope.
Collocation: suivre un cours (attend a class) and au cours de (during/in the course of). Polysemy requires contextual discernment.
Word family: affaire (business matter) → affairé (busy with business). négoce reinforces commercial sense; all share 'business' semantic field.
Word family: nom (noun) → nommer (to name/appoint) → renommer (to rename). Prefix re- indicates repetition or renewal.

members.gloss: to name; to appoint; to nominate

note: Semantic field: effet (effect/result) → efficace (able to produce effect) and résultat (concrete result). Reinforces cause-effect relationships.
Semantic nuance: arriver has dual sense (arrive/happen), survenir is 'to happen suddenly'. sur- prefix adds sense of unexpectedness or superimposition.

members.gloss: to arrive; to happen; to occur
to occur; to happen (unexpectedly); to supervene

note: Polarity and likelihood: possible (feasible) vs probable (more likely) vs impossible (not feasible). Distinction: possible is absolute, probable is modal.
Function expressions: fonction (function), servir à (to serve/be useful for), utile (useful). Equation: servir à = être utile pour.

members.gloss: to serve; to be useful; to function

note: Temporal hierarchy: an vs année (both 'year', but année emphasizes duration), mois (month). Hierarchical time units aid temporal expression.
Word family: paraître (to appear) → apparence (appearance). Related: sembler also means 'to seem' but paraître adds 'to appear/come into view'.

members.gloss: to appear; to seem; to look

note: Quantity adverbs: tant (so much, neutral), beaucoup (much/many, positive), trop (too much, negative/excessive). Tonal difference despite similar magnitude.

members.gloss: so much; so many; as much

note: Poetry terminology: vers (verse line), strophe (stanza), poésie (poetry overall). Context needed to distinguish vers (direction) from vers (verse).
Gradation of necessity: besoin (basic need) vs avoir besoin de (expression of need) vs exigence (demand/requirement). exigence is more prescriptive.

members.gloss: to need; to have need of

note: Directional verbs: aller (go away) vs venir/revenir (come toward). revenir = re + venir. Spatial orientation crucial for understanding.

members.gloss: to go; to move; to proceed

note: Method/manner terms: moyen emphasizes 'tool/means', façon/manière emphasize 'manner/style'. All express 'how', but with subtly different focuses.
Relationship/connection terms: rapport (relationship/report/ratio), relation (relationship/account), proportion (ratio/proportion). All overlap; context disambiguates.
Visual/viewpoint terms: vue (sight/view), spectacle (impressive sight), perspective (viewpoint/outlook). All involve 'seeing' or 'viewpoint' but differ in emphasis.
Quantity adverbs expressing magnitude: tant (so/as much, neutral/modal) vs beaucoup (much/many, affirmative). Often interchangeable but different registers.

members.gloss: so much; so many; as much

note: Permission/allowance verbs: laisser (to let, more permissive) vs permettre (to permit, more formal). laisser + inf = 'let do'; permettre à de = 'allow to'.

members.gloss: to leave; to let; to allow
to allow; to permit; to enable

note: Command chain: ordre (command/order) → commander (to command) → obéissance (obedience). ordre also means 'sequence/orderliness'.

members.gloss: to command; to order; to lead

note: Spatial opposition: devant (in front) vs arrière/derrière (behind). devant functions as prep/adv, arrière as noun, derrière as prep/adv.
Gift/exchange verbs: donner (to give, active) vs recevoir (to receive, passive). accepter emphasizes consent vs recevoir emphasizes reception.

members.gloss: to give; to grant; to offer
to receive; to accept; to get
to accept; to agree; to take

note: Q&A framework: question/demande (query/request) → répondre (to answer/respond). Distinction: question is informational, demande is transactional.

members.gloss: to answer; to respond; to reply
